Chalk, glass and light: what Reims and Paris taught this site

The look of this site borrows from two French cities: chalk cellars and cathedral glass in Reims, limestone and gallery white in Paris.

Reims gives the chalk: a warm white that is never clinical, and the deep blue of stained glass. Paris gives the limestone and the way a good gallery hangs a work with a small label and a lot of air around it.

So the pages here are chalk and stone, the accent is cobalt, the labels are small and numbered like works on a wall, and the projects sit on a shelf as books you take down and open.

This journal will also carry the landscapes and the small things around me that make me want to make things. They arrive as I film them.
